what: Ericsson makes mobile network equipment: radio base stations, antennas and the software that runs mobile networks, plus enterprise services and patent licensing. It is Swedish and one of only three large Western suppliers.
customers: Mobile operators worldwide, with North America its largest market, plus enterprises and handset makers paying patent royalties.
money: radio access network equipment and software
core networks, operations software and services
private networks and the Vonage communications platform
moat: Patents essential to mobile standards that earn royalties from every handset maker, plus deep integration into operators' networks that makes swapping suppliers a multi-year project.
risks: Mobile operator capital spending has been weak worldwide
The Vonage acquisition was written down heavily
Revenue has been flat over three years
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: Revenue grew about 14% last year with a 16% operating margin
Return on invested capital of 20% after restructuring
Patent licensing provides high-margin revenue regardless of equipment sales
watch: Networks segment sales in North America and operating margin.
